The escalator is 80 feet high, and your height increases from 0 at the start (when your scale is at the bottom) to 10 feet when it reaches a certain point. We will consider this rate of change over a fixed time increment (say, one second for simplicity).

We start by assuming that you are constantly moving up the escalator scale. The rate \(R\) should be such that in every second, you gain another 10 feet of height (from 0 to 10 feet) plus the escalator itself gains 80 feet in height because the escalator scale is also moving uniformly.
